theme: European tourism statistics tooling: Eurostat tour_occ / tour_ce clients, INE Spain Frontur Egatur EOAT tourist-apartment tables, ISTAT, INSEE, Destatis, ONS travel, Portugal INE

candidates.name: eurostat/pyrostat
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Eurostat Python API (in development since 2017, ~56 commits) for querying/searching/downloading any Eurostat database table via the REST/JSON web services and bulk-download facility, incl. RAMON metadata code lists. No tourism-specific dataset bundled, but tour_occ_* / tour_ce_* codes are pullable generically. EUPL-1.1 license.
candidates.why_useful: Direct, official-org-maintained way to pull Eurostat's monthly tour_occ (occupancy, nights spent) and tour_ce (demand) tables programmatically and point-in-time (vintage snapshots possible via repeated pulls), addressing the 150-day-lag limitation noted for our existing tour_ce_omr pull by making refresh trivial. Complements gap 4/17 (nowcasting, vintages).
candidates.time_coverage: current Eurostat database, historical depth same as source
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: we already hold Eurostat tour_ce_omr pulled data; this is a better/official acquisition method, not new data

candidates.name: rOpenGov/eurostat
candidates.what_it_holds: Mature R package (1,433 commits, 255 stars, on CRAN) to search/download/manipulate/visualize any Eurostat dataset by code, including tour_occ_* and tour_ce_* tourism series, with local caching.
candidates.why_useful: Well-tested, widely cited (rOpenGov ecosystem) generic Eurostat client; could be used to build a point-in-time tour_occ / tour_ce puller in R as an alternative to a hand-rolled pull, and to grab longer historical vintages of the same series we already hold.
candidates.size_hint: R package, no committed tourism data
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: acquisition method for data we already partly hold

candidates.name: eurostat/restatapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Eurostat R package (435 commits) using SDMX to search/retrieve full or filtered Eurostat datasets, TSV and SDMX formats, with caching. General-purpose, not tourism-specific in the README examples.
candidates.why_useful: Alternate official SDMX route into tour_occ/tour_ce tables with finer partial-download control (useful for pulling only e.g. NUTS2 accommodation-nights subsets without downloading whole bulk files).

candidates.name: ondata/opensdmx
candidates.what_it_holds: Python CLI/library (771 commits, MIT) for any SDMX 2.1 REST API, with built-in providers for Eurostat, ISTAT, OECD, ECB, World Bank; semantic search of dataflows, CSV/Parquet/JSON output, saved queries for reproducibility.
candidates.why_useful: Single tool that can pull Eurostat tour_occ/tour_ce AND Italy's ISTAT tourism tables (arrivals/presences by region, 'Movimento dei clienti negli esercizi ricettivi') from one client — useful for building a repeatable, versioned (saved-query) point-in-time puller across two of our target agencies at once.

candidates.name: khaeru/sdmx (sdmx1, fork of pandaSDMX)
candidates.what_it_holds: Mature Python implementation of SDMX 2.1/3.0 standard (2,570 commits, 47 stars, Apache-2.0), supporting World Bank, IMF, Eurostat, OECD, UN REST services; converts to pandas. This is the successor/fork lineage of the well-known pandaSDMX project.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose but production-grade SDMX client; can hit Eurostat tour_occ/tour_ce and OECD tourism tables, with pandas-native output for a nowcasting pipeline (MIDAS/DFM per gap 17). More actively maintained than the original pandaSDMX.

candidates.name: bis-med-it/pysdmx
candidates.what_it_holds: BIS-maintained 'opinionated' Python SDMX library, part of the sdmx topic cluster alongside eurostat/restatapi and ondata tools.
candidates.why_useful: Another actively maintained (BIS-backed) SDMX client that could substitute for a hand-rolled Eurostat/ISTAT puller; institutional backing suggests longevity.

candidates.name: InseeFrLab/pynsee
candidates.what_it_holds: Official INSEE lab Python package (1,900 commits, MIT) with 'quick access to more than 150,000 macroeconomic series' plus local data and SIRENE company registry, from INSEE and IGN APIs. No tourism-specific dataset called out in the README, but INSEE's macro series catalogue includes hotel/tourist-accommodation occupancy ('fréquentation touristique') series reachable through the same generic series-code interface.
candidates.why_useful: If France-specific tourist accommodation occupancy or consumer-spend-adjacent series are wanted for the EMEA regional split, this is the maintained, official client rather than scraping insee.fr; also usable for the France leg of gap 6 (consumer spend panels).

candidates.name: InseeFrLab/DoReMIFaSol
candidates.what_it_holds: INSEE lab tool for downloading data directly from the INSEE website (companion to DoReMIFaSolData package).
candidates.why_useful: Secondary/alternate INSEE download tool in case pynsee's API coverage misses a specific tourism-adjacent table.

candidates.name: cutterkom/destatiscleanr
candidates.what_it_holds: Small R package (14 commits, MIT) that cleans raw downloaded Destatis/GENESIS and Regionalstatistik.de files (German encoding, decimal marks, multi-line headers). README itself says it is largely obsolete since Destatis added direct CSV/API download in 2020. No tourism table specifically named.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — only useful if pulling older-format Destatis exports of German accommodation statistics (Beherbergung im Reiseverkehr / GENESIS table 45412) that predate the API. Flagged mainly because it is the only Destatis-cleaning tool found.

candidates.name: pipeworx-io/mcp-destatis
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server (4 commits, MIT) exposing Destatis GENESIS-Online search and table retrieval (population, GDP, CPI, employment, foreign trade, production) to AI agents; part of a larger 'Pipeworx' 1476-source gateway.
candidates.why_useful: Generic GENESIS-Online access point; would need testing whether it can reach German tourism/accommodation tables (45412-series) — not confirmed from README. Low confidence, early-stage repo.

candidates.name: aeturrell/real-time-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo that scrapes/aggregates real-time UK ONS datasets AND their revision histories ('revision triangles') into tidy Parquet files, config-driven (config.toml lists included series), GitHub-Actions-automated weekly updates. MIT license, 14 commits so far. Exact series list/time coverage not visible from README alone — needs a config.toml check.
candidates.why_useful: This is exactly the ALFRED-style point-in-time vintage tooling gap 4 calls out, but for UK data instead of US: if ONS travel/tourism or consumer-card-spend series are in its config, it gives ready-made vintage (as-first-published vs revised) series for the EMEA regional model without building vintage capture from scratch.
candidates.time_coverage: ongoing weekly capture, historical depth per ONS series
candidates.size_hint: Parquet files, config-driven, small repo (14 commits)

candidates.name: rgllm/awesome-portugal-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated awesome-list (512 stars, ~476 linked resources) of Portuguese open-data sources. Directly links: INE Portugal's official statistics API (https://www.ine.pt/xportal/xmain?xpid=INE&xpgid=ine_api), Turismo de Portugal's open-data portal (https://dadosabertos.turismodeportugal.pt/), the national tourism enterprise registry (https://registos.turismodeportugal.pt/), and Pordata municipal/EU statistics (https://www.pordata.pt/).
candidates.why_useful: One-stop index confirming Portugal's national tourism statistics office (INE) has a documented, token-free REST/webservice API, and that Turismo de Portugal runs its own open-data portal — both plausible sources for Portugal-specific nights/occupancy series feeding the EMEA regional split. The repo itself holds no data, just curated links.

candidates.name: rOpenSpain/Siane
candidates.what_it_holds: R package to represent Spanish INE statistical data on official Spanish administrative maps (choropleth), pulling from INE and IGN. General-purpose, not tourism-specific; no Frontur/Egatur/EOAT mentioned explicitly.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms rOpenSpain ecosystem has INE-linked mapping/data tooling; could be adapted to visualize/pull regional tourist-apartment (EOAT) figures if INE exposes them through the same generic series interface, but not verified.

candidates.name: dnme-minturdep/turismo_internacional
candidates.what_it_holds: R Shiny dashboard from Argentina's national Ministry of Tourism statistics directorate (DNMyE) covering international inbound/outbound tourism flows and the tourism trade balance across transport modes (SINTA system). Likely bundles source CSVs feeding the dashboard (typical for these Shiny repos), though exact files not confirmed from the listing alone.
candidates.why_useful: Off-Europe but hits gap 7 directly (LatAm regional travel volume, Argentina named explicitly): an official national-ministry GitHub with programmatically-built international tourism series, maintained by the same DNMyE org that also runs 'armonizacion' (harmonization of provincial tourism stats) and 'calendario_dnmye' (a SINTA release calendar — useful for point-in-time release-date tracking, gap 4).
candidates.time_coverage: current SINTA series, historical depth unconfirmed
candidates.size_hint: R Shiny app repo, unconfirmed data file sizes
candidates.license: unspecified (org uses GPL-3.0 on sibling repos)
candidates.last_activity: unspecified, org active through 2026 per topic hits

candidates.name: dnme-minturdep/armonizacion
candidates.what_it_holds: 48-commit Distill/R site titled 'Harmonización de las Estadísticas de Turismo en las Provincias' (harmonizing Argentina's provincial tourism statistics), hosted at armonizacion.yvera.tur.ar; a companion technical-document repo (DT6_ciencia_de_datos_turismo) from the same org documents the methodology in TeX.
candidates.why_useful: Government methodology + likely underlying provincial-level tourism data for Argentina, feeding LatAm regional-split forecasting (gap 7); worth a follow-up clone-free look at the repo's data/ folder for committed CSVs.

candidates.name: statistikat/STATcubeR
candidates.what_it_holds: R interface to Austria's STATcube REST API and data.statistik.gv.at (Statistics Austria's open-data portal), found via the sdmx topic cluster.
candidates.why_useful: Austria isn't in our explicit gap list but is a Eurostat-reporting EU tourism market (Vienna short-term-rental regulation is already tracked); this gives a programmatic route to Austrian accommodation-statistics tables if the regional model is extended.

notes: WebSearch tool was already at its session-wide 200/200 quota before this scout started (shared budget across the whole cataloguing sweep) — zero WebSearch calls succeeded. Fell back to WebFetch on Bing/DuckDuckGo (both returned JS-shell content with no real result links) and settled on github.com/topics/<tag> pages, which render as static HTML and worked reliably, plus direct repo README fetches. github.com/search?q=... consistently returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited), so true full-text GitHub search was not available in this modality for this run — a real gap. KEY FINDING: no dedicated GitHub repo exists for Spain's INE Frontur/Egatur/EOAT (tourist apartments) tables specifically — the 'frontur' topic has zero repos, github.com/topics/spain and /ine surfaced nothing tourism-specific, and the rate-limited /search endpoint couldn't be used to check harder. This looks like a genuine void: Frontur/Egatur data is likely only reachable via INE's raw web tables/CSV downloads, not via any community client or mirror — worth flagging to a human for a possible manual/API-key approach later, and worth another scout re-attempting github.com/search once the session-wide WebSearch/GitHub rate limits reset. Same near-void for ISTAT tourism-specific data (only generic SDMX clients that CAN reach it, not a tourism-committed dataset) and ONS travel (nothing tourism-specific under /topics/ons; aeturrell/real-time-data is the best lead but its actual series list is unconfirmed — a next agent should read its config.toml). Eurostat is the one area with multiple solid, actively-maintained official clients (pyrostat, rOpenGov/eurostat, restatapi) though none bundle committed tour_occ/tour_ce data — they are pull-methods only, so 'why not just use our existing Eurostat pull' applies to all of them; their marginal value is mainly point-in-time automation (gap 4) and easier historical backfill. Recommend a follow-up scout try `gh search` (once available) or WebSearch (once quota resets) specifically for 'frontur', 'egatur', 'apartamentos turisticos españa dataset', and 'ISTAT movimento clienti esercizi ricettivi github' — these terms were never actually search-queried, only topic-page-browsed, because of the tooling outage.
